column1: # corpus-census-ts.tsv — the PINNED TypeScript census roster.  SOUNDNESS R663 / R744 / R767.
# THE FOREIGN ARM IS NOW MEASURABLE ON 8 OF THE 28 ENTRIES, AND WAS UNMEASURABLE ON ALL 28 BEFORE —
# SOUNDNESS R767, closed by installing dependencies rather than by any scan change.  With NO
# `node_modules` anywhere in the roster the engine minted, over all 28 entries, **0 dispatch keys
# naming a dependency-owned abstraction, 0 R521 hand-off registrations and 0 supertypes resolved
# into a dependency** — against 34,273 LOCAL dispatch charges in the same runs.  The foreign arm was not
# rare here; it was absent by construction, and a reach of 0 over this roster was a statement about
# the roster.  With dependencies installed on 8 entries (13,826 of the roster's 39,396 analysed
# units) the same engine mints **1,629 foreign dispatch charges over 121 distinct dependency-owned
# keys, on 6 of those 8 entries**, plus 10 R521 hand-off registrations on 2 of them.
# SO THE HONEST HEADLINE IS NOT "THE FOREIGN ARM IS RARE".  It is: the foreign arm is ORDINARY in
# real TypeScript and was invisible to this roster.  Any R512 / R524-foreign / R521 / R613 figure
# taken over an entry whose column 8 reads `-` is still UNMEASURED, not safe.
# COLUMN 8 IS THE DEPENDENCY STATE AND COLUMN 9 IS THE FOREIGN-ARM DENOMINATOR — the same division
# of labour as columns 5 and 6, one level out.  Column 8 says HOW the deps were installed (what it
# would take to reproduce); column 9 is what the ENGINE actually resolved, and only column 9 licenses
# a foreign-arm number.  The two come apart, measured on this very roster: **rxjs has 632 packages
# installed and a foreign reach of 0**, because its 27 `class X implements <@angular/core iface>`
# sites live in `docs_app/`, a sub-project with its OWN package.json that a root install never
# touches.  `ioredis` is the same shape for a different reason — 414 packages, every foreign
# supertype resolved, and not one dispatch through a dependency-owned interface.  A test for
# `node_modules/` on disk would have called both dependency-resolvable and been wrong.
# COLUMNS 6 AND 7 ARE RECORDED IN THE DEPENDENCY STATE OF COLUMN 8, AND THEY MOVE WITH IT.  Measured
# on the 8: rows 2091 -> 1789 (nest, -14%), 54 -> 81 (vscode-languageserver-node, +50%), 209 -> 199
# (apollo-server), and nest's ANALYSED count moved 5427 -> 5448 as well.  Both directions occur, so
# an entry re-measured in the other dependency state will NOTE against this file rather than agree.
# That is why column 8 is beside them and not in a separate note.
# WHAT THE INSTALLS COST AND WHAT THEY REFUSED, because "install the deps" is not one operation:
#   npm-ci       rxjs, apollo-server, vscode-languageserver-node, node-slack-sdk, ioredis — the
#                lockfile installs exactly and is not rewritten, so the pinned tree stays clean and
#                the entry REPRODUCES.
#   npm-install  socket.io — `npm ci` REFUSED at the pinned sha (`Missing: puppeteer-core@24.43.1
#                from lock file`): the committed lockfile is out of sync with the committed
#                package.json.  A fresh resolve installed it and rewrote package-lock.json, so this
#                entry does not reproduce byte-for-byte.
#   npm-legacy   nest — `npm install` REFUSED with ERESOLVE (@apollo/server 5.5.1 against the root's
#                graphql 17.0.2 through @nestjs/graphql); installed with `--legacy-peer-deps`, which
#                is a different resolution from the one the repo's CI uses.
#   pnpm-frozen  typeorm — npm refuses this repo OUTRIGHT: `devEngines.packageManager` names pnpm
#                with `onFail: error`, so `npm ci` and `npm install` both exit EBADDEVENGINES.
#                Installed with `pnpm install --ignore-scripts --frozen-lockfile`.
# Every install ran with `--ignore-scripts`: these are third-party packages acquired to be ANALYSED,
# never to be run.  The pinned sha moved on none of them (`rev-parse HEAD` re-checked after each).
# AND A PNPM-INSTALLED TREE MINTS ITS FOREIGN KEYS UNDER THE PACKAGE NAME `.pnpm` — which is why
# typeorm's 10 keys are recorded and simultaneously not usable.  candor-ts's `declModule` takes the
# FIRST `node_modules/<seg>/` on a declaration's path, and pnpm's real path is
# `node_modules/.pnpm/yargs@17.7.2/node_modules/yargs/…`, so every dependency in the tree collapses
# into one namespace.  Held constant against npm on identical sources and identical versions:
# `yargs#Argv.option` under npm, `.pnpm#Argv.option` under pnpm.  Filed for candor-ts, not fixable
# here.  12 of the 28 entries carry a pnpm lockfile, so this is the majority installer in the
# roster, not a corner.
# GIT-PINNED, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.  The obvious shape was an npm
# roster matching java's Maven arm.  Measured 2026-09-27 over five widely-depended-upon packages at
# their published latest — axios 1.20.0, chalk 6.0.1, commander 15.0.0, yargs 18.2.0, zod 4.6.5 —
# FOUR OF THE FIVE SHIP ZERO NON-DECLARATION TYPESCRIPT.  They publish `dist/*.js` plus `*.d.ts`;
# only zod ships its sources.  candor-ts parses `/\.[mc]?tsx?$/` and EXCLUDES `.d.ts` on purpose
# (`scan.mjs:1496`; the comment at `:1493` says why — a declaration file has no bodies), so an npm
# roster would have been ~80% HOLLOW, and a hollow corpus prints 0/0/0, byte-identical to a change
# that is correctly inert.  TypeScript source lives in repositories, so the roster pins repositories.
# THE SHA IS THE PIN, NOT THE TAG.  A tag can be force-moved; `corpus-census.sh ts` clones the tag and
# REFUSES when `rev-parse HEAD` does not equal the sha here.  That is this arm's sha1.
# COLUMN 6 IS THE DENOMINATOR.  COLUMN 5 IS NOT, AND CONFLATING THEM IS THIS ROSTER'S OWN R666.
# The first cut of this file recorded only the on-disk `.ts` count and called it fitness — which is
# the java roster's mistake one level deeper: sha1 proves integrity, a file count proves presence,
# and NEITHER proves the engine will analyse it.  candor-ts selects files through the TYPESCRIPT
# PROJECT (tsconfig `files`/`include`), so measured on the first engine pass:
#     sindresorhus/execa        119 .ts files on disk  ->  analysed  1, rows 0   (impl is .js)
#     octokit/rest.js            42 .ts files on disk  ->  analysed  2, rows 1
#     apollographql/apollo-server 110 .ts files        ->  analysed  0, rows 0   (rc=2, REFUSED)
# All three passed a structural fitness check with room to spare.  execa and rest.js are DROPPED;
# apollo-server is kept with a TARGET of `packages/server`, where the same sha analyses 377 units.
# That is what column 4 is for — a monorepo root is often not a TypeScript project.
# NOT DONE, and named rather than left to be discovered: execa would likely be recoverable with
# `--allow-js`, and rest.js with a narrower target.  Neither was pursued, so neither is in the roster.
# Do not add a line without running the engine over it.  `bash bin/corpus-census.sh ts --check`
# verifies sha and structural fitness; `--measure` re-runs the engine and refuses when an entry's
# analysed count collapses, which is the only check that would have caught the three above.#
# COLUMN 8 / COLUMN 9, AND THE CHECKS THEY BUY.  `corpus-census.sh ts --check` reads column 8 against
# the disk: an entry that CLAIMS a dependency state and has no `node_modules` is BAD, because that is
# exactly the R767 shape — a roster asserting a resolvability the corpus does not have, whose
# foreign-arm figures then read as safely-inert zeros.  `--measure` re-derives column 9 from the
# report and treats a COLLAPSE to 0 as BAD for the same reason it treats a collapsed analysed count
# as BAD: the entry still counts toward the roster while contributing nothing, and the percentage
# moves the flattering way in silence.
# HOW COLUMN 9 IS DERIVED, so it can be recomputed rather than trusted: the DISTINCT `dispatchesOn`
# keys in the report whose namespace (the part before the `#`) is neither the scanned package itself
# nor a node platform module — the same boundary `isPublishableForeignIface` draws in candor-ts.
# Distinct keys rather than charges: the key is the join surface ⟨0.39⟩ obligation 3 names, and the
# charge count varies with call sites while the surface does not.
# WHAT COLUMN 9 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COUNT, because the detector for it could not be calibrated:
# the UNION rows a local implementor publishes.  Measured on three probes (a @types-typed dependency
# and an own-typings one, by the direct `implements` path and by R521's hand-off, the reach probe
# confirming `R521-REACH nominal unstorage#Driver` fired), those rows are published under a BARE
# `Iface.member` key — `Driver.hasItem`, not `unstorage#Driver.hasItem` — which is byte-identical to
# the key a LOCAL interface of the same name gets, and the roster's own entries hold 744 such rows
# with no dependencies installed at all.  So union rows cannot be split into local and foreign by key
# shape, and a count of them would have been a number that could not fail.  The consumer-side keys in
# column 9 CAN be split, which is why they are what the column records.
# NOT INSTALLED, AND WHY IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT: the other 20 entries stay at `-` deliberately.  The
# 8 were chosen because their source dispatches through abstractions a DEPENDENCY owns — measured
# before installing, by resolving each `interface X extends <imported>` / `class X implements
# <imported>` back to the import that introduced it and dropping self-references, tsconfig path
# aliases (drizzle's 124 `~/…` are all local) and workspace siblings that a `paths` mapping makes
# local anyway (nest maps `@nestjs/common` -> `./packages/common`, so its 86 `implements CanActivate`
# sites are LOCAL and its real foreign reach is fastify and rxjs).  Cost, for whoever extends this:
# ~3.0 GB of disk (df around each install) and between 333 and 1,590 packages per entry.
